DIAGNOSIS:

1) ACUTE GASTROENTERITIS WITH DEHYDRATION
2) URINARY TRACT INFECTION

HISTORY: C/O Multiple episodes of loose stools, 2-3 episodes of vomiting,
fatigue since 3 days and fever since yesterday.
Initially she was treated at local clinic.

PAST HISTORY: K/C/O Thyroid disorder on treatment.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:

PR-89/min, BP-130/80 mmHg, RR-20/min, SPO2-98" at room air.
CNS-Conscious Oriented

CVS-S1S2(+)

RS-B/L NVEBS(+)

PA-Soft, non tender

INVESTIGATIONS:

Reports Enclosed

COURSE IN THE HOSPITAL:

Patient presented to us with above mentioned complaints. After evaluation, she
was admitted to ward. Initial investigations showed normal CBC, Serum
creatinine (1.64me/dl) done was elevated. Serum electrolytes done showed low
serum sodium( 128.00mnol/L). Urine routine done showed ketone bodies(+), 10-
l2/hpf of pus cells, 13-20/hpf of epithelial cells with presence of bactreia hence
urine culture and sensitivity sent- report awaited. She was treated with IV fluids,

IV antibiotics, 1V PPI's, ['V antiemetics and other supportive measures. USG
abdomen and pelvis done showed Grade-I fatty liver changes and mildly
edematous part of ascending colon upto the hepatic Mlexure- could represent
colitis. Repeat Serum Creatinine(1.17?mg/dl) done was normal. TSH and Free
T4 done were normal. Stool routine done showed 2-4/hpf of red blood cells,
plenty/hpf of pus cells. Patient was adviced to stay back for further
management but attenders not willing to the same, hence being discharged al

request with following advice.

Hemodynamically stable
